page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-96 is a memory-dense compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors providing 48 physical cores and 96 virtual cores through multithreading with two threads per core. It features 768 GB of total system RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions (F, VNNI, and BF16) alongside SHA_NI and AES cryptographic instructions. The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators or bundled local NVMe storage, requiring persistent storage to be provisioned via remote block storage.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier computational throughput across multi-core and single-core test suites. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 111594.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 26419.0, both placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated cloud instances. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 278.64 GB/sec, while write operations reach 150.08 GB/sec. Data processing tasks demonstrate strong capacity, registering 152.44 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 37266.11 on PassMark database operations, and 101.53 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves 53.64 tokens per second during text generation on medium 7B parameter models.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on the complete absence of local storage disks and dedicated GPUs, which shifts disk throughput dependency to network storage volumes. In exchange, the instance delivers high memory capacity and dense parallel compute capability without the added cost of GPU accelerators. This hardware profile is aligned with large-scale in-memory databases, Redis clusters, high-concurrency compilation tasks, continuous integration workloads, data transformation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise application serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-96 is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 768 GB of RAM, it provides an 8 GB per vCPU resource ratio. The server lacks dedicated GPUs and local ephemeral storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk access. In performance evaluations, the system recorded a PassMark CPU score of 111594.66, a Geekbench multi-core score of 26419.0, and 152.44 million operations per second on Redis SET tests, placing within the top 10 percent. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 278.64 GB/sec, supporting data-dense parallel computing. With hardware support for AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, the instance is structured for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, in-memory caching layers, massive relational or key-value databases, and large-scale data engineering workflows.
